request: Jack, 10 November 2026 (T3 thread): starting with the homepage of the nov10-logo-clarity version (https://6b5c2f00.hqc-london.pages.dev, commit 3f212df), significantly improve UI, UX, motion design and conversion so the page feels like a beautiful, dynamic journey rather than a wall of text, without changing or removing any copy. Use the council (three independent model reviewers) until the standard is met. Follow-up, Jack, 11 November 2026 (same T3 thread): make the homepage far more image-led with deliberate photographic section backgrounds instead of gradients; remove semicolons from the copy where they appear; make motion and scroll animation feel completely smooth and never buggy; vary positioning so content is not always on the left; split sections where it helps and make each section more immersive and less chunky, following the conventions of award-winning service-business sites; diagnose and fix what is missing from the hero.

requirements.text: Planning: freeze this scope on the nov10-logo-clarity line; earlier accepted Phase 8 requirements (logo round L1/L2, F1-F3, copy restoration, imagery) stay in force.
Homepage only: significantly improve presentation, layout rhythm and motion design (entrance choreography, scroll-linked motion, interactive states) so the page reads as a guided journey.

Raise conversion potential: clearer CTA hierarchy, persistent access to the existing primary actions, a stronger service-selector interaction and less friction, reusing only existing on-page CTA labels.

Preserve every word of homepage copy (visible text, alt text, aria labels, title and meta), its order, every link destination, data-track attribute, selector routing and conversion event. A mechanical text comparison against the baseline must show no changed, removed or reordered copy.
Honour prefers-reduced-motion, keep all content readable without JavaScript, avoid layout shift and LCP delay, keep keyboard and screen-reader behaviour, and add no new runtime dependencies.
Leave every other page, shared component, form, CRM routing, tracking, schema, redirect, every image and the Phase 8 production hold unchanged.
Record the resulting version in revisions/versions.json (and the review room) before handover; full npm run check:revision passes.

Image-led homepage (Jack, 11 Nov): each major section gets a deliberate photographic treatment (full-bleed bands, split media, image-led cards) using only existing library images under public/images, no image repeated on the page, no decorative gradients, glows or orbs; readability overlays are flat tints.
Copy punctuation (Jack, 11 Nov): homepage list items render without trailing semicolons or full stops; no other copy changes. This is the only authorised exception to D3.

Layout and motion (Jack, 11 Nov): vary alignment and composition across sections (centred, right, split, full-bleed), split sections where it clarifies, diagnose and fix the hero (one decisive image, clear hierarchy, routes in view), and make all motion smooth: no jitter, no late pop-in, no cursor gimmicks; scroll effects run on transform and opacity only.

Homepage-only component: rail progress, drag and reveal.

preserve: All homepage copy and its order, alt text, aria labels, links, data-track attributes, selector results copy, routing and events, except the C8 list punctuation.

Desktop and mobile browser checks of every homepage section, the service selector journey, reduced-motion and no-JS rendering, and console health.
Council review by three independent model reviewers (Claude, GPT, DeepSeek) with scores, repeated after fixes.

Round 5: mechanical copy comparison against 8f5331b shows only the C8 punctuation removals plus the existing dock labels; desktop, laptop and phone captures of every section; scroll-through recordings checked for jank; independent Codex review.
